info.name: Gymnasyum Backend API
info.description: Ordered happy-path and negative API verification flow for the Gymnasyum backend. Run with the local environment against a development database seeded with the demo admin and catalog service records.

request.description: Public health probe. Expected: HTTP 200 with status "ok".
Public customer registration. Expected: HTTP 200 on first run; HTTP 409 if the demo email already exists.

exec: pm.test("response status is expected", function () { pm.expect([200, 409]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Customer login. Expected: HTTP 200; saves accessToken and refreshToken.
Negative invalid-login case. Expected: HTTP 401.

Diagnostic seed prerequisite check only. Expected: HTTP 409 because admin@example.com must already be seeded. If HTTP 200 is returned, registration created a customer, which is intentionally never saved as an admin token; seed the admin account before running Login Admin.

exec: pm.test("fallback registration did not create an admin", function () { pm.expect(body.user && body.user.role).to.eql("customer"); });

pm.test("seeded admin prerequisite is available", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code, "Admin seed is missing: registration returned a customer (HTTP 200); seed the admin account before Login Admin").to.eql(409); });

request.description: Seeded admin login. Expected: HTTP 200 with role "admin"; saves admin tokens only after the role assertion passes. Requires the seeded admin account.

exec: pm.test("Login Admin returned the seeded admin role", function () { pm.expect(isAdmin, "Login Admin requires a seeded admin account; received role: " + (body.user && body.user.role)).to.eql(true); });
pm.test("access token exists for the admin account", function () { pm.expect(isAdmin && body.accessToken, "Admin token was not saved because the response user was not an admin").to.be.ok; });

pm.test("refresh token exists for the admin account", function () { pm.expect(isAdmin && body.refreshToken, "Admin refresh token was not saved because the response user was not an admin").to.be.ok; });

request.description: Refresh token rotation. Expected: HTTP 200; replaces both tokens.
Protected admin identity read. Expected: HTTP 200.
Invalidate the seeded admin refresh token. Expected: HTTP 200 with success true; uses the admin bearer token and does not overwrite token variables.
Negative role check. Customer uses admin-only route. Expected: HTTP 403.
Negative ownership check. Customer attempts to read the seeded admin user. Expected: HTTP 403.
Admin user list. Expected: HTTP 200 with an array.
Admin reads seeded customer user. Expected: HTTP 200.
Admin updates the seeded customer user name. Expected: HTTP 200 with the updated user record.

exec: pm.test("updated user id exists", function () { pm.expect(body.id).to.not.be.undefined; });
pm.test("updated user name is returned", function () { pm.expect(body.name).to.eql("Postman Customer Updated"); });
pm.test("updated user remains a customer", function () { pm.expect(body.role).to.eql("customer"); });

request.description: Customer reads own member profile. Expected: HTTP 200; saves memberId.
Customer updates own profile. Expected: HTTP 200.

exec: pm.test("updated member id exists", function () { pm.expect(body.id).to.not.be.undefined; });

request.description: Admin member list. Expected: HTTP 200.
Admin reads customer member. Expected: HTTP 200.
Negative role check. Customer cannot create coaches. Expected: HTTP 403.
Admin coach list. Expected: HTTP 200.
Admin creates coach associated to seeded service. Expected: HTTP 200; saves coachId.
Admin updates coach. Expected: HTTP 200.

exec: pm.test("updated coach id exists", function () { pm.expect(body.id).to.not.be.undefined; });

request.description: Admin creates active package. Expected: HTTP 200; saves packageId.
Admin updates the package created by the preceding request. Expected: HTTP 200 with the updated package record.

exec: pm.test("updated package description is returned", function () { pm.expect(body.description).to.eql("Five coached sessions, updated by Postman"); });

request.description: Customer catalog read. Expected: HTTP 200.
Negative validation case. Expected: HTTP 422.
Admin creates capacity-one source schedule. Expected: HTTP 200; saves scheduleId.
Admin creates target reschedule. Expected: HTTP 200; saves targetScheduleId.

exec: pm.test("target schedule id exists", function () { pm.expect(body.id).to.not.be.undefined; });

request.description: Admin updates the source schedule created by the preceding request. Expected: HTTP 200 with the updated schedule record.

exec: pm.test("updated schedule title is returned", function () { pm.expect(body.title).to.eql("Postman Morning Yoga Updated"); });

request.description: Customer schedule read. Expected: HTTP 200.
Negative validation case. Expected: HTTP 422.
Customer creates pending payment. Expected: HTTP 200; saves paymentId.
Customer own payment list. Expected: HTTP 200.
Negative role check. Expected: HTTP 403.
Admin marks pending payment paid. Expected: HTTP 200; creates subscription and saves subscriptionId.
Admin payment list. Expected: HTTP 200.
Customer subscription read after payment is marked paid. Expected: HTTP 200.

exec: const body = pm.response.json(); pm.test("created subscription is present", function () { pm.expect(body.some(function (item) { return item.id === pm.environment.get("subscriptionId"); })).to.eql(true); });

request.description: Customer books source schedule. Expected: HTTP 200; saves bookingId.

request.description: Negative full/duplicate booking case. Expected: HTTP 409.
Negative malformed identifier case. Expected: HTTP 422.
Customer own booking list. Expected: HTTP 200.
Admin booking list. Expected: HTTP 200.

item.name: Chatbot Reschedule
item.description: Dedicated chatbot reschedule flow. Run after the authentication, coach, package, payment, subscription, booking, and schedule setup requests in this collection. It creates separate schedules and a separate booking so it cannot conflict with the direct Reschedule Requests flow. Configure the server process with GEN_AI_MODE=stub for deterministic recommendations; the Postman environment value documents that setting only. The folder temporarily isolates the pre-existing direct target schedule and has an explicit cleanup request that restores its captured original status. Postman has no finally hook: run this folder without Newman --bail, and if execution is interrupted before cleanup, run Cleanup: restore direct target schedule manually before the direct flow.

request.description: Creates the dedicated chatbot source schedule. Expected: HTTP 200; saves chatSourceScheduleId. Requires server GEN_AI_MODE=stub for the deterministic message assertion.

exec: pm.test("chat source schedule id exists", function () { pm.expect(body.id).to.match(/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/i); });

request.description: Creates the dedicated chatbot target schedule. Expected: HTTP 200; saves chatTargetScheduleId.

exec: pm.test("chat target schedule id exists", function () { pm.expect(body.id).to.match(/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/i); });

request.description: Books the dedicated chatbot source schedule using the existing active subscription/package setup. Expected: HTTP 200; saves chatBookingId.

exec: pm.test("chat booking uses the dedicated source", function () { pm.expect(body.scheduleId).to.eql(pm.environment.get("chatSourceScheduleId")); });
pm.test("chat booking is booked", function () { pm.expect(body.status).to.eql("booked"); });

request.description: Starts a chatbot session for the dedicated booking. Expected: HTTP 201; saves chatSessionId.

exec: pm.test("session has the exact fields", function () { pm.expect(Object.keys(body).sort()).to.eql(["bookingId", "createdAt", "currentIntent", "id", "proposedScheduleId", "status", "updatedAt"]); });
pm.test("chat session uses the dedicated booking", function () { pm.expect(body.bookingId).to.eql(pm.environment.get("chatBookingId")); });

item.name: Admin capture direct target original status

request.description: Pre-step before fixture isolation. Reads all schedules, captures the existing direct-flow target status in directTargetOriginalStatus, and refuses to continue the isolation step if the target is missing. This value is used by cleanup instead of assuming available.

exec: const target = schedules.find(function (item) { return item.id === pm.environment.get("targetScheduleId"); });
pm.test("direct target exists before isolation", function () { pm.expect(target).to.not.be.undefined; });
pm.test("direct target status is restorable", function () { pm.expect(["available", "full", "cancelled"]).to.include(target.status); });

item.name: Admin isolate direct target from chatbot candidates

request.description: Fixture isolation: temporarily cancels the existing direct-flow target schedule so StubGenAiClient's first available candidate is deterministically the dedicated chat target. The direct target is restored at the end of this folder before the existing Reschedule Requests folder runs; direct request definitions are unchanged.

exec: pm.test("direct target is isolated from chatbot candidates", function () { pm.expect(body.id).to.eql(pm.environment.get("targetScheduleId")); pm.expect(body.status).to.eql("cancelled"); });

item.description: Fixture isolation: temporarily cancels the existing direct-flow target schedule so StubGenAiClient's first available candidate is deterministically the dedicated chat target. The preceding capture request stores the exact original status in directTargetOriginalStatus. Its pre-request guard skips cancellation if capture did not succeed.

request.description: Sends a reschedule message. Expected with GEN_AI_MODE=stub: HTTP 200, exact Reschedule intent, awaiting_confirmation, and the dedicated target in recommendedSchedules.

exec: pm.test("turn has the exact top-level fields", function () { pm.expect(Object.keys(body).sort()).to.eql(["analysis", "assistantMessage", "session", "userMessage"]); });
pm.test("turn session has the exact fields", function () { pm.expect(Object.keys(body.session).sort()).to.eql(["currentIntent", "id", "proposedScheduleId", "status"]); });
pm.test("user message has the exact fields", function () { pm.expect(Object.keys(body.userMessage).sort()).to.eql(["content", "id", "role"]); });
pm.test("assistant message has the exact fields", function () { pm.expect(Object.keys(body.assistantMessage).sort()).to.eql(["content", "id", "role"]); });
pm.test("analysis has the exact fields", function () { pm.expect(Object.keys(body.analysis).sort()).to.eql(["confidence", "intent", "recommendedSchedules"]); });

pm.test("recommended schedule has the exact fields", function () { pm.expect(body.analysis.recommendedSchedules).to.have.length(1); pm.expect(Object.keys(body.analysis.recommendedSchedules[0]).sort()).to.eql(["endsAt", "id", "startsAt"]); });

pm.test("proposed schedule and recommendation are the dedicated target", function () { pm.expect(body.session.proposedScheduleId).to.eql(body.analysis.recommendedSchedules[0].id); pm.expect(body.session.proposedScheduleId).to.eql(pm.environment.get("chatTargetScheduleId")); });

request.description: Explicit cleanup request. Restores the direct-flow target to the exact status captured in directTargetOriginalStatus, rather than hardcoding available. Postman has no finally hook; run this folder without --bail, and run this request manually if execution stops before cleanup.

exec: pm.test("direct target is restored for the direct flow", function () { pm.expect(body.id).to.eql(pm.environment.get("targetScheduleId")); pm.expect(body.status).to.eql("available"); });

request.description: Negative confirmation guard. Confirms the source instead of the proposed target; expected HTTP 409 with error code CONFIRMATION_MISMATCH. This does not alter the happy-path session.
Confirms the chatbot's proposed target schedule. Expected: HTTP 201; exact submitted response shape and a pending chat reschedule request; saves chatRescheduleId.

exec: pm.test("confirmation has the exact top-level fields", function () { pm.expect(Object.keys(body).sort()).to.eql(["message", "rescheduleRequest", "sessionId", "status"]); });

pm.test("pending request has the exact fields and dedicated tuple", function () { pm.expect(Object.keys(body.rescheduleRequest).sort()).to.eql(["bookingId", "chatSessionId", "fromScheduleId", "id", "status", "toScheduleId"]); pm.expect(body.rescheduleRequest.bookingId).to.eql(pm.environment.get("chatBookingId")); pm.expect(body.rescheduleRequest.chatSessionId).to.eql(pm.environment.get("chatSessionId")); pm.expect(body.rescheduleRequest.fromScheduleId).to.eql(pm.environment.get("chatSourceScheduleId")); pm.expect(body.rescheduleRequest.toScheduleId).to.eql(pm.environment.get("chatTargetScheduleId")); pm.expect(body.rescheduleRequest.status).to.eql("pending"); });

request.description: Reads the submitted chatbot session. Expected: HTTP 200 with the exact session response fields.
Reads chatbot messages. Expected: HTTP 200 and the captured user message remains present.

exec: pm.test("messages are an array", function () { pm.expect(body).to.be.an("array"); });
pm.test("every message has the exact fields", function () { body.forEach(function (item) { pm.expect(Object.keys(item).sort()).to.eql(["content", "id", "role"]); }); });
pm.test("captured chat message is present", function () { pm.expect(body.some(function (item) { return item.id === pm.environment.get("chatMessageId"); })).to.eql(true); });

request.description: Lists pending requests and verifies the chatbot request tuple is pending. Expected: HTTP 200.

exec: pm.test("pending response is an array", function () { pm.expect(body).to.be.an("array"); });
const request = body.find(function (item) { return item.id === pm.environment.get("chatRescheduleId"); });

pm.test("pending request has the documented exact fields", function () { pm.expect(request).to.not.be.undefined; pm.expect(Object.keys(request).sort()).to.eql(["adminNote", "bookingId", "chatSessionId", "createdAt", "customerMessage", "fromScheduleId", "id", "memberId", "reviewedAt", "reviewedBy", "status", "toScheduleId", "updatedAt"]); });

pm.test("chat request is listed as pending", function () { pm.expect(request.status).to.eql("pending"); pm.expect(request.chatSessionId).to.eql(pm.environment.get("chatSessionId")); pm.expect(request.bookingId).to.eql(pm.environment.get("chatBookingId")); pm.expect(request.fromScheduleId).to.eql(pm.environment.get("chatSourceScheduleId")); pm.expect(request.toScheduleId).to.eql(pm.environment.get("chatTargetScheduleId")); });

item.name: Customer verify chat booking remains on source

request.description: Verifies the booking has not moved before admin review. Expected: HTTP 200 and chatBookingId remains on chatSourceScheduleId.

exec: const booking = pm.response.json().find(function (item) { return item.id === pm.environment.get("chatBookingId"); });
pm.test("chat booking exists before approval", function () { pm.expect(booking).to.not.be.undefined; });
pm.test("chat booking is still on the source", function () { pm.expect(booking.scheduleId).to.eql(pm.environment.get("chatSourceScheduleId")); pm.expect(booking.status).to.eql("booked"); });

request.description: Approves the chatbot request. Expected: HTTP 200 with approved status; the subsequent booking read verifies the booking moved to chatTargetScheduleId.

exec: pm.test("approved response has the documented exact fields", function () { pm.expect(Object.keys(body).sort()).to.eql(["adminNote", "bookingId", "chatSessionId", "createdAt", "customerMessage", "fromScheduleId", "id", "memberId", "reviewedAt", "reviewedBy", "status", "toScheduleId", "updatedAt"]); });

pm.test("approved request retains the dedicated tuple", function () { pm.expect(body.chatSessionId).to.eql(pm.environment.get("chatSessionId")); pm.expect(body.bookingId).to.eql(pm.environment.get("chatBookingId")); pm.expect(body.fromScheduleId).to.eql(pm.environment.get("chatSourceScheduleId")); pm.expect(body.toScheduleId).to.eql(pm.environment.get("chatTargetScheduleId")); });

item.name: Customer verify chat booking after approval

request.description: Optional post-approval verification. Expected: HTTP 200 and the dedicated booking is now on chatTargetScheduleId.

exec: const booking = pm.response.json().find(function (item) { return item.id === pm.environment.get("chatBookingId"); });

pm.test("approved chat booking moved to target", function () { pm.expect(booking).to.not.be.undefined; pm.expect(booking.scheduleId).to.eql(pm.environment.get("chatTargetScheduleId")); pm.expect(booking.status).to.eql("booked"); });

request.description: Customer requests reschedule. Expected: HTTP 200; saves rescheduleId.
Negative role check. Customer cannot review. Expected: HTTP 403.
Admin request list. Expected: HTTP 200.
Admin reviews request. Expected: HTTP 200 with approved status and reviewer.
Customer cancels the booking after the reschedule flow completes. Expected: HTTP 200 with cancelled status. The endpoint has no request fields; an empty JSON object is sent explicitly.
Customer own request list. Expected: HTTP 200.

exec: const body = pm.response.json(); pm.test("approved request is present", function () { pm.expect(body.some(function (item) { return item.id === pm.environment.get("rescheduleId"); })).to.eql(true); });
